title: Cognitive Walkthrough
body:
A **cognitive walkthrough** steps through one specific task, one action at a time, asking the
same four questions at every step. It targets learnability, meaning how a first-time user copes
with no training.

```
At each step:
  1. Will the user be trying to achieve this effect?
  2. Will they notice that the correct action is available?
  3. Will they recognise that this control produces the effect they want?
  4. After acting, will they see that progress was made?
```

Question 2 is about the [[Signifier]] and question 4 is about [[Feedback]], so the method is a
structured way of applying those concepts to a real sequence, where a screen examined in
isolation would pass.

It differs from [[Heuristic Evaluation]] in scope. A heuristic evaluation inspects the
whole interface against general principles, and a walkthrough follows one task in depth, which
is what lets it catch a step where the user has no reason to expect the next action even though
every screen is individually well designed.

Both are expert methods, so both are cheaper than [[Usability Testing]] and neither
replaces it, since both predict what a user will do and neither observes one.
